  PROBLEM: The body-length check treats any 100-record activity response as evidence that older activity was not read, although it cannot distinguish a complete 100-record history from a truncated page.
  WHY: The request sets a page size of 100 but the response body alone does not establish that another page exists; reviewers characterized this as NIT.

  WHY: If the SHA remains unavailable across ticks, the path continues retrying the merge attempt and logging warnings.

  PROBLEM: The gate reports “older activity was not read (reason=activity_page_full)” whenever the activity response contains 100 records, even when the repository has exactly 100 activity records total.
  WHY: The request uses `per_page=100`; when the branch has exactly 100 activity records, the response is complete, but the code checks `length >= 100` and reports that older activity was not read. The runtime behavior (fail closed, page once) is correct; only the alert text is misleading in this edge case.
